summary: Tested device-binding state machine + logout-lock end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass (first-bind→same-device→different-device→pending→approve→409 re-approve→reject→reset→owner-bypass→/me logout_enabled toggle). Frontend /admin/employees: device-requests-banner renders with employee_name/email/model/device_id snippet, DEVICE column shows 'bound' with Smartphone icon, emp-logout-toggle flips OFF→ON with toast 'Logout locked/enabled for Sample Employee' and persists across reload, emp-reset-device button appears only when device is bound, device-approve-{id} clears the row from the banner immediately, regression Send selfie / Notify / Edit / Remove buttons still present.
critical_code_review_comments: mobile.py device_bind: On a repeat bind of the CURRENTLY bound device, the response omits first_bind (correct), but on a re-bind of a different-device that was previously APPROVED, the code sets bound_device_id and returns {status:'authorized'} — no first_bind flag. Fine but worth documenting.
employees.py list_device_requests: Missing pagination and no filter for a specific employee — small orgs are fine but the banner will pile up if many pendings accumulate.
employees.py approve_device_request: 'superseded' status is used for cancelled peers, but reset_device uses 'cancelled'. Two similar terminal statuses — consider harmonising to a single vocabulary.

auth.py /me: Silently defaults logout_enabled=False when the user doc lookup fails. If u is None (user deleted mid-request), returning face_enrolled=False + logout_enabled=False is safe but the caller can't distinguish 'locked' from 'user missing'. Minor.
EmployeesManage.jsx toggleLogout: onError toast shows the axios error but the UI state isn't rolled back optimistically (there is no optimistic update, so this is actually safe — just noting).

device_requests collection: no unique index on (org_id,user_id,device_id,status='pending'). A racing duplicate device/bind could in theory create two pending rows for the same device — currently handled by 'sort desc + status != pending' guard, so benign.

seed_data_creation: Test file uses per-run uuid-suffixed device_ids (DEV-TEST-{A|B|C}1-<runid>) so it is idempotent across runs. During UI test, seeded UI-DEV-A1 (bound) and UI-DEV-B2 (pending, then approved and set as bound). Cleanup at end: employee 6a6f63fda37a01476b2c4cca is now unbound (bound_device_id=None) and logout_enabled=false. Approved/rejected device_request rows remain in DB (harmless per main agent's note).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_device_binding.py -o addopts='' — must disable xdist because the state-machine tests share state across TestDeviceBinding→TestAdminReview classes (approval flow expects pending record from the previous class). All 12 pass single-worker. UI checks used data-testids: device-requests-banner, device-req-{id}, device-approve-{id}, device-reject-{id}, emp-device-{id}, emp-logout-toggle-{id}, emp-reset-device-{id}. Owner bypass verified: POST /api/mobile/device/bind as org_owner always returns {status:'authorized'} without touching device_requests.
